testerFailure.how: The row's flex container is md:flex-nowrap; the heading is min-w-0 with content width and the directory was md:flex-1 md:basis-0 with min-w-0, so at md the heading's content squeezed the directory to zero. The directory now carries md:min-w-48, a floor the name cannot take, and its md:truncate is gone so the shortened text is read whole rather than ellipsised — the architect's condition that assertWhole hold over it. The tester's red row passes unmodified.

filesChanged: packages/dispatch/web/src/features/agents/AgentsPage.tsx — md:min-w-48 on the directory span, md:truncate dropped, the comment saying why the floor exists and what it is sized for

packages/dispatch/e2e/agents.e2e.ts — the row at :1717 only: its laptop branch now asserts the directory is visible and passes assertWhole, which is what let a zero-width element through before. The tester's row at :1807 is untouched

packages/claude-envoy/src/envoy-channel-server.ts — restoreRole awaited with a catch of every failure, one stderr line naming the file and the reason
trickyParts: md:truncate had to go, not just the floor: Tailwind's truncate sets text-overflow: ellipsis unconditionally, and e2e/unclipped.ts's assertWhole flags a computed ellipsis whether or not the text is actually being cut. With the floor in place the shortened text fits anyway, and a host or segment wider than the floor now wraps inside it rather than being cut, with the whole path still the title.

The floor is 192 px (md:min-w-48), a token already used elsewhere in this package. It is sized for a host and a last segment at text-xs; the directory holds exactly 192 px at 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440, because the heading takes everything else at each of them.
deviations: The architect offered two mechanisms — a floor on the same line, or letting the directory fall to its own line above the phone breakpoint — and left the choice to me. I took the floor: it keeps the shortened '<host> · <last segment>' text with the full path in its title, which is what agents.e2e.ts:1717 expects, so that row stays true and nothing about the laptop row's shape drifts.
